radiology_report:
Radiology Section | Leiden University Medical Center | 28 Feb 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical Context: Elevated PSA (6.5 ng/mL) with a normal digital rectal examination. Assessment for clinically significant prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
Glandular volume registers at 80.6 mL. T2-weighted sequences display a peripheral zone with uniform intermediate signal intensity, devoid of focal hypointensities. The transition zone exhibits moderate benign prostatic hyperplasia accompanied by slight median lobe prominence. A minute 4 mm benign cyst resides within the right mid-gland transition zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows no areas of restricted diffusion. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal neither early nor focal enhancement. Seminal vesicles, neurovascular bundles, and pelvic lymph nodes remain unremarkable. No suspicious focal lesion is identified.

IMPRESSION:
1. Benign prostatic enlargement measuring 80.6 mL.
2. No PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion identified.
3. PI-RADS 2.
4. PSA density 0.081 ng/mL/mL.
5. csPCa predicted probability 0.0.

previous_notes.text: Laboratory data from May 2023 indicate a PSA of 5.1 ng/mL, reflecting a rise from the 4.2 ng/mL value documented in July 2022. Digital rectal examination remained unremarkable. The clinician noted the steady increase during the consultation.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: A subsequent measurement in April 2024 recorded 5.7 ng/mL, maintaining the upward trend. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms persist, though the patient reports no other complaints. Clinical correlation was arranged.
